public_rationale: The primary records support substantial parts of Marcus's statement: OpenAI, Inc. obtained federal exemption, submitted a California charity registration, and explicitly reported a safety-focused mission benefiting humanity. They also support reading his reference as the nonprofit parent. However, this evidence package does not directly establish continued registration and exemption through May 30, 2024. Nor does the IRS letter identify safe deployment as a specific determination supporting exemption. These gaps prevent a complete finding; they are not evidence that Marcus was wrong.
limitations: The conclusion concerns the completeness of the retrieved evidence, not a finding that exemption or registration had lapsed.
The legal documents were read through third-party copies.
A declared safety mission does not establish actual safe conduct or IRS approval of particular products.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is a registered nonprofit receiving tax-exempt status based on its promise to deploy AI safely.

statement.excerpt: But OpenAI has been and continues to be a California-registered 501(3)(c) nonprofit, pledged not to profits, but to humanity – and still getting tax-exempt status on the basis of their promise to deploy AI safely:
statement.document_title: Disturbing and misleading efforts to defame Helen Toner through misdirection

from_speaker: has been and continues to be
pledged not to profits, but to humanity
tax-exempt status on the basis of their promise to deploy AI safely
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion of the nonprofit board identifies OpenAI, Inc., the nonprofit parent, as the subject.
Read '501(3)(c)' as an inadvertent transposition of 501(c)(3).

The ordinary reading is that OpenAI held charitable tax-exempt status while its declared charitable mission included safe AI benefiting humanity. This does not assert that the IRS certified its products as safe.
For the ongoing state, examine the latest publicly reported annual period before the post, calendar 2022, and its continuation through May 30, 2024.
California registration does not mean California incorporation.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish that OpenAI, Inc. remained a California-registered, federally tax-exempt nonprofit through the post date, with safe AI benefiting humanity included in its declared exempt-purpose activities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish that the nonprofit lacked the claimed registration or exemption at the relevant time, or that the claimed safety and public-benefit purpose was absent from its exempt-purpose filings.

evidence.excerpt:
We're pleased to tell you we determined you're exempt from federal income tax
under Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Section 501(c)(3).
evidence.locator: IRS determination letter dated November 3, 2016, opening paragraph
evidence.publisher: Internal Revenue Service; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence.explanation: The IRS granted the claimed federal exemption. The letter was included in the California registration package received in August 2017; it does not separately certify safe AI deployment.

evidence.excerpt:
We enclose the initial registration of OpenAI, Inc., a Delaware nonprofit nonstock
corporation which qualified to do business in California on January 7,2016, pursuant to
Government Code Section 12585.
evidence.locator: Adler & Colvin registration cover letter, August 24, 2017
evidence.publisher: Adler & Colvin, on behalf of OpenAI, Inc.; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence.explanation: The submission establishes the California registration history and distinguishes it from Delaware incorporation. An initial submission alone does not establish the registry's status in May 2024.

evidence.excerpt:
OpenAI’s mission is to build general-purpose artificial intelligence (“AI”) that safely

benefits humanity, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return.
evidence.locator: 2022 Form 990, Schedule O, response to Part I, line 1
evidence.publisher: OpenAI, Inc.; copy hosted by Gwern
evidence.explanation: The latest annual filing publicly available before the post expressly combines safety, humanity's benefit, and freedom from a requirement to generate financial returns. The same return identifies OpenAI, Inc. as exempt under 501(c)(3).

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated IRS and California records confirming status through May 30, 2024, together with the exemption application and charitable-purpose filings linking that status to the declared safety and public-benefit activities.
